note: The web-reading record of `lib/attestation.mjs`. `base` is one issuer value-up page, read, filed through observation_file on a previous run, and therefore citable now; each scenario shallow-merges its `overrides`. Every URL is on `example.invalid` so nothing here can be fetched, and no company named is a recommendation.

base.claim: 이사회가 2026~2028년 총주주환원율 50%를 목표로 결의했다고 회사가 스스로 밝힌다.

scenarios.name: a-document-read-and-filed-round-trips
scenarios.why: The control. Five fields plus the id the host returned, and the grade that travels with it says whose word this is.

scenarios.name: a-search-result-summary-never-makes-a-candidate
scenarios.why: #305 in as many words: 검색 결과 제목이나 요약만으로 후보를 확정하지 않는다. Without the document's URL, its publication date and the instant this desk read it, what is recorded is a summary of a document nobody here opened.

scenarios.name: a-publication-date-nobody-has-is-the-same-refusal
scenarios.why: The half of the rule that catches the plausible case: a real URL, opened, with no date on it. Korean policy and IR pages recur annually with near-identical wording, so an undated one is last year's plan as often as this year's.

scenarios.name: an-excerpt-over-the-cap-is-refused-and-never-trimmed
scenarios.why: A hash taken over a fragment filed as a whole document leaves an auditor who fetched the URL unable to tell a trimmed row from a fabricated one. The host refuses it; checking here buys the run a sentence before the round trip rather than after it.

scenarios.name: an-excerpt-exactly-at-the-cap-is-accepted
scenarios.why: So that what is refused above is the overrun and not the cap being read one character short.

scenarios.name: a-search-results-page-is-not-a-document
scenarios.why: A page whose content changes with the query is a URL an auditor cannot go back to.

scenarios.name: a-homepage-is-not-a-document-either
scenarios.why: The same failure at the other end: a page whose content changes with the day.

scenarios.name: a-source-type-outside-the-four-is-refused
scenarios.why: An issuer's own words, a newspaper's summary of them and this desk's interpretation of that summary are three different weights, and a record that cannot say which lets an interpretation be filed at a filing's weight.

scenarios.name: this-desks-own-reading-has-a-type-of-its-own
scenarios.why: `manager-interpretation` is in the closed set precisely so that an interpretation can be filed honestly rather than dressed as a company announcement.

scenarios.name: a-document-published-after-as-of-is-not-evidence-for-it
scenarios.why: The point-in-time rule, and `observation_file` refuses it on the host side too.

scenarios.name: an-id-minted-this-run-is-carried-and-not-cited
scenarios.why: Host gap H-4: evidence filed during a run that has not ended is not committed to the Kernel until the run finishes, so an id from observation_file is citable in run N+1. That is why candidate.evidenceIds is a carried field.

scenarios.name: a-reading-nobody-filed-is-an-absence-and-not-a-refusal
scenarios.why: It is a well-formed reading that has not been through the round trip yet. `unevaluated`, so the run is told to file it rather than being stopped.

scenarios.name: a-reading-that-says-nothing-is-refused
scenarios.why: A reading is filed for something. Without the claim it supports, a later run has a URL and no idea what this desk took from it.
